requests.text: Kasliwal J. separately reasoned that the expired licence, fire-related vacating and absence of force or unlawful dispossession defeated Section 6 restoration in these circumstances. This is his opinion only, not the Bench's unified holding; the contrary opinion and referral remain unresolved in this document.

Ramaswamy J. separately relied on the concession, retained intention to possess and due-process protection of settled possession to uphold Section 6 restoration on his analysis. This is not a unified Bench merits decision or resolution of the regular lease/licence and title controversy.

counterarguments: IK-1144022:L104-L109 versus IK-1144022:L165-L168: Kasliwal read the fire, bank letter and no-force key delivery as loss without unlawful dispossession; Ramaswamy interpreted a limited repair-related handover, retained furniture and the later exclusion as dispossession without consent.

IK-1144022:L68-L69 and L140-L141 versus L166-L167: Both opinions report counsel proceeding on alleged dispossession for the suit; only Ramaswamy treated the concession as precluding denial, and the source alternates between with-prejudice and without-prejudice wording.

IK-1144022:L106-L118 versus L209-L210 and L240-L243: Kasliwal used the expired licence, trespasser characterization and admitted ownership against restoration; Ramaswamy treated longstanding settled possession as protected from self-help regardless of expiry, and reserved lease/licence classification.

IK-1144022:L75-L85 and L142-L143: The High Court ordered restoration despite criticism of the bank’s conduct, limited its conduct observations to prima facie, stayed implementation ten weeks and reserved title-based claims; its order was not a unanimous appellate merits determination.

IK-1144022:L153-L164, L142, L252: Section 6 requires non-consensual dispossession outside due course within six months and excludes Government suits, while ordinary appeal/review limitations do not eliminate Article 136 review on Ramaswamy’s analysis; no one condition alone proves entitlement.

IK-1144022:L126, L253 and L257: The judges proposed incompatible appellate dispositions, followed by a larger-bench referral; neither individual outcome proves the inputs or resolves the Bench conflict.

IK-1144022:L69, L143 and L251: Candidate role unification is not harmless: a company-made concession (E02 actor) differs from bank-protection merits findings (E01 protected subject); the R2 applications globally designate E02 as protected subject, and the R1 exact-match candidate attempts to equate P14’s actor with E01.
